text: By dawn on Tuesday, the Marisol Trench probe had slipped to 9,400 metres, the deepest descent yet recorded in the yearlong Pelagia survey. Mission director Irena Vale said the craft, lowered from the research barge Halcyon Star, passed the trench’s broken limestone terraces and entered a zone of near-total blackness shortly after 04:10 local time. The ascent route was plotted against charts first drawn in 1978, when the trench was only a wavering line at the edge of maritime maps. Engineers aboard the vessel reported steady telemetry, though pressure readings rose sharply beyond 9,000 metres. For the team, the milestone was less a triumph than a reminder of how little remains known beneath the sea’s oldest wounds.
